stories.title: Blackstone Snaps Up Ken Griffin’s 125 Worth Avenue in Palm Beach for $86M
stories.excerpt: Billionaire Ken Griffin just parted ways with his last remaining retail property on Worth Avenue in Palm Beach, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. Blackstone Real Estate has agreed to acquire the three-story office and retail building at 125 Worth Avenue, owned by Griffin since 2023, for $86 million in an all-cash deal, sources familiar with the trade said. Griffin previously bought the roughly 50,000-square-foot property from Dreyfuss Management and Frisbie Group for $83 million in 2023. “High-street retail continues to experience strong fundamentals, and Palm Beach represents one of the highest performing luxury retail markets in North America,” Elena Clarfield, principal at Blackstone Real Estate, told Commercial Observer. Indeed, as a retail corridor, the world famous Worth Avenue enjoys extreme scarcity when it comes to supply, coupled with soaring demand from a deluge of high-income residents into Palm Beach. Limited supply has also driven up property valuations in the prestigious area, evidenced by Acadia Realty Trust’s March 2026 acquisition of 225 Worth Avenue, leased to Gucci, for $43 million, or more than $4,329 per square foot. Blackstone declined to comment further but sources said the firm now intends to renovate the property, upgrading both the retail and office components to better align them with the continued evolution of Worth Avenue, a high-scale shopping district that’s home to several luxury tenants including Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Ferragamo and Van Cleef & Arpels. Representatives for Griffin could not immediately be reached for comment. The transaction represents Griffin’s second disposition on Worth Avenue in under a year. Last November, the billionaire sold his 48,578-square-foot property at 151 Worth Avenue to the family of GoldenTree Asset Management financier Steven Tananbaum, Commercial Observer reported at the time. bullets: Blackstone acquires 125 Worth Avenue, Palm Beach for $86M all-cash.
Ken Griffin flipped property in 3 years: $83M buy (2023) → $86M sale.
Worth Avenue luxury retail faces extreme scarcity; valuations driven by high-income migration.
stories.summary: Blackstone Real Estate acquired 125 Worth Avenue in Palm Beach, a 50,000-square-foot office/retail building, for $86 million in an all-cash transaction. Ken Griffin, who purchased the property in 2023 for $83 million, exited the asset with minimal gain. The deal reflects Blackstone's confidence in Palm Beach's ultra-luxury retail fundamentals, driven by soaring demand from high-income residents migrating into South Florida and constrained supply on the world-famous shopping corridor.
stories.impact: This deal is primarily distressed-asset/hospitality-focused and does not materially signal apartment demand or development opportunity in Palm Beach. Luxury retail is supply-constrained by nature and does not correlate to multifamily fundamentals; however, the underlying driver—sustained high-income in-migration to South Florida—does support multifamily demand in South Florida markets (Miami, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach) for both market-rate and high-end rental product targeting this demographic.

stories.title: Steel Peak Acquires Seattle-Area IOS Property
stories.excerpt: Steel Peak has acquired an industrial outdoor storage (IOS) property located at 1031 4th Avenue North in Kent, Washington, for $9 million.This is Steel Peak’s fourth IOS property acquisition in the Seattle area in the past 12 months and 15th overall. Will Schmidt of CBRE represented Steel Peak in its acquisition.“This acquisition checks a lot of the boxes we look for in IOS,” said Blake Rodgers, Principal at Steel Peak. “The property sits in a dense, infill industrial location in the Kent Valley with direct visibility from Highway 167, making it a site that would be extremely difficult to replicate today.”1031 4th Avenue North is ideally located, enabling efficient north-south freight movement throughout the Puget Sound region. The 3.09-acre property includes a 23,515-square-foot industrial building featuring five oversized grade-level doors, seven bridge cranes, approximately 2,500 square feet of office space, and a fully paved and fenced yard. bullets: Steel Peak acquires Kent, WA IOS property for $9M; 4th Seattle-area deal in 12 months.
Industrial outdoor storage property at 1031 4th Avenue North, Highway 167 visibility.
15th IOS acquisition overall signals consolidation and investor appetite for Seattle industrial.
stories.summary: Steel Peak acquired an industrial outdoor storage (IOS) property in Kent, Washington for $9 million, marking its fourth acquisition in the Seattle area within the past 12 months and 15th overall. The property benefits from dense infill location, direct Highway 167 visibility, and irreplaceable site characteristics. The rapid pace of acquisitions reflects strong capital appetite for industrial real estate in the Pacific Northwest.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, Steel Peak's aggressive Seattle industrial acquisition pace signals robust logistics and e-commerce demand in the Puget Sound region, which correlates with sustained job growth and population in-migration that supports apartment demand in Seattle/Bellevue/Renton submarkets. Industrial expansion typically precedes residential demand growth in secondary markets.

stories.title: California Awards $239M in Gap Funding to 20 Affordable Projects
stories.excerpt: Gov. Gavin Newsom announced nearly $239 million in construction-gap funding for 20 affordable multifamily developments across California. The projects underwent a streamlined approval process to keep development on track and cut red tape, according to the governor’s office. With project costs totaling more than $1.2 billion, the development will bring 1,700 affordable units to market. The awards follow April’s announcement from the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) for a Multifamily Housing Program Gap Funding Notice of Funding Availability. The projects awarded have not yet received tax-exempt bond financing or low-income tax credits. “This innovative funding solution directly confronts cost challenges that have stalled critically needed affordable housing communities in California,” said HCD Director Gustavo Velasquez. “I am tremendously proud that our team could use the streamlined processes we have developed to make these projects whole so quickly.” Pictured: Eden Housing’s Downtown Livermore Apartments, one of the 20 projects selected for gap funding. The post California Awards $239M in Gap Funding to 20 Affordable Projects appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: California awards $239M gap funding to 20 affordable multifamily projects; 1,700 units total.
Projects total $1.2B cost; streamlined approval process cuts development timeline/red tape.
Units lack tax-exempt bonds and LIHTCs; gap funding bridges financing gap to completion.
stories.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom announced $239 million in construction-gap funding for 20 affordable multifamily developments across California, enabling 1,700 affordable units with total project costs exceeding $1.2 billion. The award follows HCD's Multifamily Housing Program NOFA and uses streamlined approval processes to accelerate closings. Projects had stalled due to financing gaps despite strong fundamentals; gap funding fills the void where tax-exempt bond financing and low-income housing tax credits were insufficient.
stories.impact: This signals California's continued appetite for affordable supply and willingness to deploy capital creatively when traditional financing fails—a tailwind for affordable developers but also a proxy for increased cost burdens stalling projects statewide. For market-rate developers, the policy affirms that California's housing shortage remains acute and multifamily supply constraints persist across metros (LA, SF Bay, Sacramento, San Diego), supporting rent growth and development feasibility for unrestricted projects. Gap funding announcements typically cluster in high-cost markets; watch project locations to identify submarkets with strongest underlying demand.

stories.title: Walmart-Anchored Retail Property in Portland Secures $14M Refinancing
stories.excerpt: Gantry has secured a $13.65 million permanent loan to refinance maturing debt for Parkway Village at Sherwood, located at 21174-21430 SW Langer Farm Parkway in Sherwood, a Portland suburb approximately 15 miles from the city center. The 45,653-square-foot center is anchored by Walmart and features tenants such as Starbucks, Chipotle, The Old Spaghetti Factory, Panera Bread, Crumbl Cookies, Club Pilates, and Legacy GoHealth Urgent Care. Gantry’s Blake Hering, Principal, and Kristin Lapinskas, Senior Associate, with the firm’s Portland production office, represented the borrower, a private real estate investor. The seven-year, fixed-rate, non-recourse loan was secured with 30-year amortization. Gantry will service the loan. “Gantry’s life company correspondents continue to be a consistent source for high-quality loans with substantial allocations available for stabilized grocery-anchored and neighborhood retail centers where debt service aligns,” said Hering. The post Walmart-Anchored Retail Property in Portland Secures $14M Refinancing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gantry secures $13.65M permanent loan to refinance Parkway Village at Sherwood, Portland.
45,653-sf Walmart-anchored retail center; 7-year fixed, non-recourse, 30-year amortization.
Life company sources remain strong for stabilized grocery/neighborhood retail; debt service aligns.
stories.summary: Gantry arranged a $13.65 million permanent loan for Parkway Village at Sherwood, a 45,653-square-foot Walmart-anchored retail center in Sherwood, Oregon (15 miles west of Portland). The seven-year, fixed-rate, non-recourse loan features 30-year amortization and was sourced from life company correspondents. Tenancy includes Starbucks, Chipotle, Panera, and healthcare providers, signaling stable neighborhood-retail fundamentals.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily. However, the successful refinancing of grocery-anchored and neighborhood retail centers signals capital availability for stabilized suburban Portland real estate and confidence in Portland's recovery post-COVID. This backstops the investment case for suburban multifamily in Portland suburbs (Sherwood, Lake Oswego, Tigard), where density and neighborhood retail anchoring support apartment rents.

stories.title: Savills Arranges Compass Health Center’s First Location in Virginia
stories.excerpt: Compass Health Center, a provider of mental healthcare, has signed a lease to occupy 22,203 square feet of space at 3160 Fairview Park Drive in Falls Church, Virginia. The Savills team of Vice Chairman Eric Feinberg, Corporate Managing Director Brandon Nasatir, Managing Director Nick DiChiara, and Executive Vice President Jon Glass represented Compass Health Center in the transaction.“Expanding into Northern Virginia is an important milestone for Compass Health Center as we continue to increase access to high-quality mental health care,” said David Schreiber, MD, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer at Compass Health Center. Compass Health Center is headquartered in Illinois, and the Falls Church location will be the company’s first physical site in Virginia. “The central location of 3160 Fairview Park Drive provides Compass Health Center with strategic access to the densely populated areas of Fairfax and Arlington counties, as well as the Washington, D.C. area,” added Feinberg. The post Savills Arranges Compass Health Center’s First Location in Virginia appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Compass Health Center leases 22,203 sf at Falls Church, VA; first Virginia location.
Headquarters in Illinois; strategic access to Fairfax, Arlington, and DC metro area.
Healthcare tenant expansion signals professional/high-income worker attraction to Northern Virginia.
stories.summary: Compass Health Center, an Illinois-based mental healthcare provider, leased 22,203 square feet at 3160 Fairview Park Drive in Falls Church, Virginia, marking its first physical site in the state. Savills represented the tenant, highlighting the property's central location within the densely populated Fairfax and Arlington county markets and proximity to Washington, D.C.
stories.impact: Healthcare provider expansion into Northern Virginia signals accelerating professional job growth and population in-migration to the Falls Church–Arlington–Fairfax corridor. This supports multifamily demand in NoVA markets (Arlington, Fairfax, Falls Church), particularly for workforce housing targeting mid-to-high income professionals. The $70–85/sf office rents typical in the Falls Church corridor suggest strong employment fundamentals that should underpin apartment demand growth in nearby residential submarkets over the next 12–24 months.

stories.title: L&G, Taurus Partner on Ground-Up Multifamily Project in Greater Boston
stories.excerpt: L&G’s Asset Management business in the U.S. has acquired a development site at 292-294 Baker Ave. in Concord, MA and plans to begin construction on a two-building, 201-unit multifamily community. The company’s first ground-up development in the U.S., the project continues L&G’s partnership with Taurus Investment Holdings, LLC. The investment is being made on behalf of L&G’s Institutional Retirement business, putting long-term retirement capital behind new U.S. housing supply and building on the firm’s recent multifamily investments in Denver and Chicago. Construction is expected to begin this fall, with the first building targeted for completion by the end of 2028 and the second expected to follow in 2029. “By acquiring the site and moving into construction on a high-quality multifamily community in 2026, we are expanding our presence in a supply-constrained Greater Boston market with a project that combines strong housing fundamentals, meaningful affordability and leading sustainability ambitions,” said Alexia Gottschalch, Head of US Real Estate Equity, L&G – Asset Management – America. “It also reflects the continued growth of our multifamily capabilities, from development through stabilized, operational assets.” The post L&G, Taurus Partner on Ground-Up Multifamily Project in Greater Boston appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: L&G Asset Management + Taurus acquire 292-294 Baker Ave., Concord, MA; 201-unit ground-up.
Construction begins fall 2026; Building 1 delivery end-2028, Building 2 2029.
Institutional retirement capital deployed; supply-constrained Greater Boston market with affordability focus.
stories.summary: L&G Asset Management (UK-listed, entering U.S. ground-up development) partnered with Taurus Investment Holdings to acquire a development site in Concord, Massachusetts for a 201-unit, two-building multifamily community. Funded by L&G's Institutional Retirement business, the project will begin construction in fall 2026, with first delivery targeted for end-2028 and second building in 2029. The investment emphasizes housing supply constraints, affordability, and sustainability in greater Boston.
stories.impact: L&G's first U.S. ground-up multifamily development and explicit targeting of 'supply-constrained' Boston signals institutional capital confidence in Northeast rental growth and supply scarcity. This validates the Boston development thesis for other developers and suggests continued investor appetite for the Boston metro despite competitive development. The Concord location (west of Boston) indicates developers are expanding beyond urban core into inner suburbs where land is cheaper and entitlements faster—a signal that Boston's constraint is pushing new supply outward, which may soften rents in the central market but support pricing in under-supplied suburban corridors.

stories.title: Fund Administrator Hanover Park Inks 19K-SF Deal at 387 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: An artificial intelligence-driven fund administrator is moving its headquarters to TF Cornerstone’s 387 Park Avenue South, Commercial Observer has learned. Hanover Park signed a 19,269-square-foot lease on the entire 10th floor of the NoMad property, marking its fifth office move in two years, according to CEO Chris Hladczuk. The firm’s most recent office address is listed on its website as 115 East 23rd Street. TF Cornerstone did not immediately provide the asking rent or the length of the lease, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $85.73 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Existing tenants are choosing to expand here and new companies are choosing to locate here,” Joe Lanzilotta, director of commercial asset management at TF Cornerstone, said in a statement. “The property continues to outperform the market as a destination for growing businesses.” It is unclear who represented the tenant in the transaction, but Cushman & Wakefield’s Ethan Silverstein handled negotiations on behalf of the landlord in the deal signed in July. It’s unclear who represented the tenant. “The combination of TF Cornerstone’s long-term investment, highly efficient 20,000-square-foot floor plates and premier NoMad location continues to resonate with tenants,” Silverstein said in a statement. “The recent leasing activity demonstrates that companies are prioritizing best-in-class buildings, and with one full floor becoming available this fall, the property remains well positioned to meet continued demand.” Other recent deals in the 230,000-square-foot building at the corner of Park Avenue South and East 27th Street include a lease for marketing firm PMG Worldwide, which expanded from the second to third floor in May and brought its total footprint there to 38,744 square feet, according to TF Cornerstone. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hanover Park, AI-driven fund administrator, leases 19,269 sf (entire 10th floor) at 387 Park Ave South.
Fifth office move in two years; headquarters relocation within Manhattan NoMad submarket.
Midtown South office asking rent ~$85.73/sf (Q2 2026); active demand from growing firms.
stories.summary: Hanover Park, an artificial intelligence-driven fund administrator, signed a 19,269-square-foot lease on the 10th floor of TF Cornerstone's 387 Park Avenue South in NoMad, marking its fifth office relocation in two years. The property's landlord highlights strong tenant retention and new-tenant attraction at the asset, with Midtown South office space averaging $85.73/sf in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, sustained office leasing velocity in Midtown South/NoMad and the presence of high-growth tech/fintech firms (AI-driven fund admin) signals continued professional employment and in-migration into Manhattan. This supports cross-asset confidence in NYC multifamily, particularly in eastern submarket (East Village, Gramercy, Murray Hill, Flatiron) residential neighborhoods adjacent to NoMad office corridors, where renter demographic (young professionals, high-income) overlaps with office tenant base.

stories.title: Peachtree Recaps Ritz-Carlton Portland With $141M C-PACE Loan
stories.excerpt: A New York lender is more than ready for a Portland hospitality resurgence. Ready Capital, which assumed full ownership of the The Ritz-Carlton Portland mixed-use project following a foreclosure in July 2025, just secured $141 million of commercial property accessed clean energy (C-PACE) debt for the recapitalization of the 35-story tower, Commercial Observer has learned. Peachtree Group originated the C-PACE loan for the 2023-completed Block 216 Tower development that features a 251-key hotel, 131 condominium units and 159,000 square feet of office space. Construction of the Ritz-Carlton-Portland, the Marriott’s brand’s first hotel in the Pacific Northwest, commenced in 2019 before encountering delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic and ensuing struggles to the city’s economy. Jared Schlosser, head of credit originations at Peachtree Group, said condo units at the property have sold at a healthy pace and the hotel is well positioned for success as one of the newest lodging offerings in the Portland region. “It’s the nicest hotel up there and that pocket of Portland is revitalizing,” Schlosser told CO. “I think there’s probably more tailwinds ahead versus headwinds for Portland.” Schlosser added that C-PACE debt was conducive for the recap since as a newer building it was developed under “stringent” building codes with much of the project eligible for retroactive financing. He noted that the deal marks Peachtree’s second largest loan. Ready Capital set the stage for owning The Ritz-Carlton Portland when it acquired a prior construction loan on the development valued at more than $500 million through a 2022 merger with Mosaic Real Estate Investors. The lender manages the property in partnership with Lincoln Property Company. Ready Capital did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ready Capital secures $141M C-PACE debt for Ritz-Carlton Portland mixed-use recapitalization.
35-story tower: 251-key hotel, 131 condos, 159,000 sf office; foreclosed July 2025.
Property completed 2023; condo sales pace healthy; market recovery bet on Portland lodging resurgence.
stories.summary: Ready Capital, following a July 2025 foreclosure, secured $141 million in commercial property accessed clean energy (C-PACE) debt for the recapitalization of the Ritz-Carlton Portland (Block 216 Tower). The 35-story mixed-use asset includes 251 hotel keys, 131 condominiums, and 159,000 square feet of office, completed in 2023. Construction had encountered COVID-19 delays and local economic headwinds; condo units are now selling at a healthy pace, signaling market recovery.
stories.impact: Mixed-use projects in Portland show distress recovery and investor confidence in Portland's turnaround. The successful C-PACE refinance and condo sales momentum suggest the Portland market (hard hit by pandemic and civil unrest) is stabilizing. For multifamily developers, this signals pent-up demand for residential in Portland, particularly in downtown and adjacent Pearl District, as corporate tenants and professional workers return. However, the condo component competing with rental supply may offset some apartment demand upside; developers should watch absorption and rental pricing in downtown Portland and East Side submarkets (Belmont, Hawthorne) where apartments may face headwinds from condo conversions.

stories.title: Office Furniture Manufacturer Haworth Renews 30K SF at SL Green’s 125 Park Avenue
stories.excerpt: Office furniture manufacturer Haworth is staying seated at 125 Park Avenue. Haworth has signed a 10-year lease renewal for its 30,365-square-foot office and showroom space at the 25-story Midtown office building, landlord SL Green Realty announced Wednesday. The company, which manufactures and sells high-end, ergonomic office seating and workspaces, has been a tenant in the property, also known as the Pershing Square Building, for more than a decade. The firm, which did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, previously renewed its lease for the same space back in 2015, CO reported at the time. The asking rent was $100 per square foot. SL Green was represented in-house in this deal, while Haworth was represented by Ethan Silverstein and Amy Zhen from Cushman & Wakefield. C&W did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “We are proud to extend our valued relationship with Haworth at 125 Park Avenue,” Steven Durels, executive vice president and director of leasing and real property at SL Green, said in a statement. “The building’s proximity to Grand Central Terminal and our new lobby and elevator cab renovation have helped maintain 99 percent occupancy.” SL Green acquired 125 Park Avenue in 2010 for $330 million, according to property records. The building sits across the street from Grand Central Terminal on Park Avenue and East 42nd Street. Other tenants in the building include banking and investment firm TD Securities and real estate brokerage Newmark. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Haworth (office furniture mfr.) renews 30,365 sf at SL Green's 125 Park Ave, Midtown.
10-year lease renewal; tenant since 2010+; SL Green's Grand Central proximity amenity cited.
Existing tenant retention and long lease duration signal office sublease/hub stability in Midtown.
stories.summary: Office furniture manufacturer Haworth renewed its 30,365-square-foot lease for an additional 10 years at SL Green Realty's 125 Park Avenue (Pershing Square Building) in Midtown Manhattan, where it has been located for more than a decade. SL Green highlighted the building's proximity to Grand Central Terminal and recent capital improvements (new lobby/elevator) as retention drivers. The renewal demonstrates stable tenancy in a prime Midtown asset.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, SL Green's ability to renew large-block office tenants at a 25-story Midtown office property signals persistent demand for premium office space in Manhattan's Grand Central corridor, supporting continued employment and professional in-migration. This backstops multifamily demand in adjacent East Midtown and Kips Bay residential markets where young professionals and renter households cluster near Midtown job centers.

stories.title: CMBS Loan Backed by Vornado, Related’s 85 10th Avenue Sent to Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: A $396 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan secured by 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-square-foot office property in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent maturity default, according to an alert from Morningstar Credit. 85 10th Avenue is owned jointly by Vornado Realty Trust and the Related Companies. Related purchased the property in 2007 from Somerset Partners for $430 million and brought Vornado in as a 50/50 partner. The $396 million loan makes up DBWF 2016-85T and is part of larger conduits CD 2017-CD3 and BACM 2017-BNK3. It is expected to default ahead of its December 2026 maturity date, according to Morningstar. The building’s largest tenant, Google, currently takes up 47 percent of its space, as the firm has gradually expanded since signing a 180,000-square-foot lease in 2014. But cash flow from rents has declined lately, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. Morningstar Credit reports that 85 10th Avenue’s cash flow fell 28 percent below underwriting in 2025, and that biometric screening company CLEAR, which signed a 120,000-square-foot lease for a new headquarters in 2021, is currently in a rent abatement period. Vornado reported that the building’s occupancy stood at 89 percent in its most recent second-quarter earnings supplemental. The 11-story 85 10th Avenue first opened in 1913 as a Nabisco factory and was redeveloped for commercial office use in the late 1990s. Vornado and Related invested into renovating the lobby in 2023. Vornado and Related did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: 85 10th Avenue (Vornado/Related, 633k sf) CMBS loan ($396M) sent to special servicing.
Imminent maturity default expected before Dec 2026; Google occupies 47% (180k sf leased 2014).
Chelsea office property experiencing cash flow decline post-COVID; refinancing/sale pressure likely.
stories.summary: A $396 million CMBS loan backed by 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-square-foot Chelsea office tower owned jointly by Vornado Realty Trust and Related Companies, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent maturity default. Google is the largest tenant, occupying 47 percent of the space on a 180,000-square-foot lease signed in 2014. Cash flow has declined since the COVID-19 pandemic, and the loan is expected to default prior to its December 2026 maturity date.
stories.impact: This flagship Manhattan office default signals continued distress in the New York City office market and likely forced refinancing, restructuring, or sale of the asset within the next 12 months. While office-focused, the deterioration of a prime Google-anchored Chelsea property underscores lasting pandemic-driven office demand loss in Manhattan; this may suppress office-to-residential conversion economics in Chelsea and Hell's Kitchen, limiting new apartment supply from adaptive reuse. However, developer opportunity exists: if 85 10th Avenue or similar distressed office towers convert to residential (condos or rentals), this could unlock meaningful supply in supply-constrained Manhattan. Watch for distressed asset sales and conversion announcements in Chelsea and West Chelsea in 2026–2027; these may signal a shift from office recovery to residential repositioning.
